title: How Markets Actually Work
promise: Why the bull and the bear never stop fighting, who you trade against, and the toll on every trade.
unlock: Tell a bull market from a bear market
Know who is on the other side of your trade
Rank the six asset classes by risk
Spot the spread you pay on every trade

questions.q: A stock fell from a high of $200 to $150 over four months. By the usual definition, is it in a bear market?
options: Yes: it’s down 25% from the high
No: bear markets need a year
questions.why: Use percent, not dollars: the $50 fall ÷ the $200 high = 25% down. That’s past the 20% line, so it’s a bear market. Time doesn’t decide it.

questions.q: Big news hits. Robots trade on it in 0.001 seconds. What’s your smartest move?
options: Race to buy in the first second
questions.why: You can’t beat a robot’s speed, and copying it means arriving late. Your edge is patience: let the rush pass and trade only if your setup appears.

questions.q: A friend wants his first investment to be steady and to pay him interest. Which class fits best?
questions.why: A bond is a loan to a government or company. It pays interest and is one of the calmest choices. Leverage and new tokens are the riskiest.

questions.q: You want to put $1,000 into a new token. Bid $0.095, ask $0.105, and only a few thousand dollars of orders on each side. What do you do?
options: The spread doesn’t matter if I hold for years
Pass, or buy small: you start about 10% down
Buy $1,000 now: at $0.10 it can only go up
questions.why: You buy at $0.105 but can only sell at $0.095, so about $95 of your $1,000 is gone at once. Holding doesn’t avoid it, and few orders make the exit worse.

refresher.title: Lesson 1 · Bulls vs bears
refresher.text: A bear market is a fall of about 20% or more from a recent high. Use percent: fall ÷ high. A $100 stock that drops to $78 is down $22 ÷ $100 = 22%.

refresher.title: Lesson 2 · Who’s on the other side
refresher.text: You can’t beat robots on speed or funds on research. Your edge is patience: let the rush pass and trade only your plan’s setups.

refresher.title: Lesson 3 · The six asset classes and their risk
refresher.text: From lower to higher risk: bonds and broad index ETFs, then stocks, commodities and forex, then crypto. Bonds pay interest and swing the least.

refresher.title: Lesson 4 · Bid, ask and the spread
refresher.text: You buy at the ask and sell at the bid. The gap × shares is what a round trip costs: $0.10 × 100 = $10.
